paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin for Agentic Control Plane: logs and checks tool calls. Ask works; deny is re
ported, not enforced yet.
# @agenticcontrolplane/dsh
Agentic Control Plane for DeepSeek Harness: every tool call is checked and logged against your polic
ies, recording what ran, what was held, and why. Ask works. Deny is reported to the agent but not ye
t enforced (see the note below).
> **Deny is not enforced yet.** When a policy says `deny`, the plugin reports it to the agent with t
he reason, but it does not stop the call today (the fix is tracked). Until that ships, treat dsh as
audit plus ask. See the coverage matrix.
> **Which ACP?** dsh also ships `packages/acp` in core. That one is Zed's Agent Client Protocol, the
editor↔agent standard, published as `@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp`. It is an unrelated project with the sam
e acronym. If you're wiring dsh into Zed or the AI SDK, you want that one; this plugin checks each t
ool call against your policies. The full map: agenticcontrolplane.com/acp-vs-acp.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Every decision also lands in your console with tool, decision, reason and latency. dsh's own Traject
ory log and your ACP activity log are two independent records of the same history. One workspace cov
ers every harness you run, so the same rules apply to dsh, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenClaw (
deny excepted, see the note above). Free for individuals.
This is a native Cordis plugin on dsh's typed interception points, not a shell-hook shim. It registe
s a native Cordis plugin on dsh's typed interception points, not a shell-hook shim. It registers on:
- `tools/pre-execute`: the policy decision. `allow` lets the call through. `deny` is reported to the
agent with the reason, but the plugin does not stop the call yet. `ask` hands off to dsh's own appr

oval flow.
- `tools/post-execute`: output scanning. A server-side block turns the result into correc
tive feedback; shadow-mode notices surface what enforcement *would* have done.

## What happens if the gateway is down
If the gateway is down, dsh keeps working, and you are told the calls weren't checked:
- **Interactive sessions fail open, loudly.** If the gateway is unreachable, the call proceeds, a `[

ACP] ⚠ UNGOVERNED` warning is logged, and a line lands in `~/.acp/lapse.log`.
- **Unattended agents

fail closed.** With nobody watching, a call that can't be checked is blocked.
- This posture only co
vers the inability to *ask* the policy. It does not change how a `deny` is handled (see the note at
inability to *ask* the policy. It does not change how a `deny` is handled (see the note at the top).
In headless compositions with no approval service mounted, dsh itself resolves `ask` to deny, so una
ttended runs cannot self-approve.
## Notes
- Already running our Claude Code hook? dsh's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code` bridge runs an un
modified `hooks.json`, so `govern.mjs` works today with zero new code. Input rewriting is not suppor

ted on that path. This native plugin is the recommended path.
- This package launched as `dsh-plugin
-acp`; that name still installs but is deprecated. Same code, so swap the name in your profile when
convenient. (The `cordis.patch.yml` in this repo still carries the old name.)

evidence.fact: 未提供访问密钥时，插件会显示警告，但允许会话继续运行。
evidence.quote: No key: the plugin prints a warning and lets the session run.

limitations: 拒绝策略目前仅报告给智能体，并不会真正阻止工具调用。
网关不可达时，交互式会话会记录未受治理警告并继续运行；无人值守代理则会在无法检查时阻止调用。
无密钥时仅警告并继续会话，不代表策略检查已经生效。
